subject: RE: Post-call: Observability & ops tooling follow-up / next tests vs hyperscalers
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Jessica Park <jessica@acme.com>, Tom Lee <tom.lee@acme.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-15T10:12:00-08:00
Subject: Post-call recap + proposed next tests (observability / ops)

Hi Jessica / Tom —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our discovery call and the concrete next steps we discussed so the team at Acme is aligned: 

What we heard:
- Primary driver: lower inference unit cost and more predictable latency for peak billing windows (checkout flows, recommendations), while keeping strong observability for tracing and per-route cost attribution.
- Current stack: in-house inference API (built on a hyperscaler-hosted GPU fleet) + Prometheus/Grafana for infra metrics, Lightstep for traces.
- Open questions: end-to-end tracing across frontend->model, token-level cost breakdowns, rollbacks for model regressions, and whether we can match your latency SLOs under burst.

Proposed next tests (high level):
1) Side-by-side perf + cost comparison vs hyperscaler-managed endpoints for a 48-hour synthetic workload that matches your peak sequences. Metrics: p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens/sec, cost per 1M tokens, and tail latency under burst.
2) Observability integration test: demo prefix/KV cache visibility, per-route token cost breakdown, and sample trace across request->inference->response that includes KV cache hits/misses.
3) Regression safety check: smoke prompts set to validate quality parity (we'll use a small eval set you agree on).

Deliverables we offered:
- A short runbook for required access (API keys, sandbox endpoints, sample payloads) — attached.
- A proposed test plan + timeline (Rishi will share the technical steps and the XLS with metrics).
- A mutual action plan (MAP) to get to a pilot in ~3 weeks if we have sandbox access.

Ask from Acme today:
- Can you share a short list of traffic patterns (typical sequence length distribution, % of requests that require retrieval/long context) and a link to a sample trace or sanitized logs?
- Who should I include for procurement/contract discussions when we get to pricing?

I attached the runbook for the observability test (redwood-runbook-observability.pdf). I also cc'd Rishi who will handle the technical coordination.

If that all looks good, I can send a one-week MAP with dates tomorrow.

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0192

Attachment: redwood-runbook-observability.pdf

From: Jessica Park <jessica@acme.com>

Date: 2026-11-15T13:04:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + proposed next tests (observability / ops)

Marissa —

Thanks for the clear recap and the runbook. This aligns with what we discussed. A few quick answers:

- Traffic patterns: average seq len ~120 tokens, 95th ~420 tokens; ~12% of requests hit the retrieval path. Peak bursts happen during daily flash sales (around 15:00 PST) and last ~20-30 minutes.
- We can provide sanitized traces from Lightstep (I'll drop a Drive link below).
- Procurement: loop in Mary Chen (mary.chen@acme.com) for contracting/pricing.

One ask from our side: can you give a rough estimate for the test cost if we run your side-by-side comparison for 48 hours? That will help Mary prioritize the spend. Also, can you confirm whether Redwood can instrument token-level cost attribution (we currently only have per-endpoint cost) — that's a key differentiator for us.

I'll also schedule a short sync with Tom (infra) and Mary next week; please include Rishi.

Thanks —
Jessica Park
Sr. Product Lead, Recommendations
Acme Corp

Drive link (sanitized traces): https://drive.google.com/file/d/1ExampleAcmeTrace

Subject: Re: Post-call recap + proposed next tests (observability / ops)

Jessica —

Appreciate the details. Quick answers while Rishi puts together the XLS test plan: 

- Rough test cost estimate: for the 48-hour side-by-side (small-medium instances, expected traffic profile you shared) ballpark is $2.5k–$5k on Redwood-hosted pilot runs. We'll provide an itemized breakdown in the MAP and the proposal.
- Token-level cost attribution: yes — Redwood provides per-route and per-token accounting in the Console; we can surface token counts, cache hit/miss costs, and an exportable CSV for cost analysis. We'll demo those panels in the observability test.

Next steps from Redwood side:
- Rishi will send the technical test plan + metrics and a recommended sandbox config (we'll include the tracing span format we suggest).
- I'll draft a 7-day MAP with target dates and send the MAA proposal PDF for Mary to review.

Rishi — can you include the tracing spans we recommend (Lightstep/OTEL compatible) and the specific Grafana dashboards we provision for the test?

Thanks —
Marissa

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
To: Jessica Park <jessica@acme.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>, Tom Lee <tom.lee@acme.com>
Date: 2026-11-17T14:40:00-08:00
Subject: Acme observability + perf test plan (technical)

Hi Jessica / Tom —

Following up with the technical plan for the observability and perf comparison. I've attached the XLS with the full matrix (acme-observability-testplan.xlsx) but the key points are below: 

Test scope (48-hour side-by-side):
- Synthetic traffic that mirrors your seq distribution (avg 120, p95 420).
- 3 load phases: steady-state (24h), burst windows (3x peak for 30min windows repeated), and spike recovery.

Metrics to capture:
- Latency: p50/p95/p99, tail over burst windows
- Throughput: tokens/sec, requests/sec
- Cost: cost per 1M tokens, cache-adjusted cost (subtract KV cache savings)
- Observability: trace spans with model invocation, KV cache hit/miss tags, db/retrieval latency, and per-request token counts
- Quality: small eval set (we'll agree on ~50 prompts) with basic BLEU/ROUGE-like checks and human spot checks for regressions

Instrumentation notes:
- Tracing: we will emit OTEL spans with the following attributes: redwood.span_type, redwood.cache_hit (bool), redwood.token_count (int), http.request_id. These map to Lightstep via OTLP sink.
- Dashboards: we will provision a Grafana folder with pre-built panels: token-cost-by-route, cache-hit-rate, span-latency-breakdown, and request-sample-traces.
- Data retention: test logs/metrics will be retained for 30 days; full traces for 14 days unless you request extended retention.

Resource / access needed from Acme:
- Sandbox API endpoint (read-only keys are fine) + a small sample of recent request payloads (sanitized).
- Name for a Tech PO who can approve the eval prompts and the 50-sample eval set.

Proposed schedule (tentative):
- Nov 18: Access provided + runbook executed
- Nov 19-20: Run tests; daily sync at 16:00 PST
- Nov 23: Results review and MAP decision call

I've attached the XLS with the metric matrix and telemetry mapping. Let me know if you'd like us to tweak retention or add any additional panels.

Thanks —
Rishi Malhotra
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
rishi@redwood.com

Attachment: acme-observability-testplan.xlsx
